capture_path.problem: capture.py renders a SceneCapture2D at full render-target resolution with its own temporal history; the game renders 83% (Epic) and TSR-upscales
capture_path.method: C:/TownChess/work/ra/c7/ra_c7cap.py (not in the repo) wraps the lead's capture.py and sets the capture component's main_view_resolution + main_view_family (ignore_screen_percentage off): the engine then forks the main view's screen-percentage interface into the capture (SceneCaptureRendering.cpp, bInheritMainViewScreenPercentage), i.e. 1594x896 -> 1920x1080 through TSR, as the player sees it at -TCShotRes 1920x1080. Log confirms r.ScreenPercentage 83, r.AntiAliasingMethod 4

ab_h1_crown.Lamp_Key cast_shadows off: GONE: floor clean and uniform (also at FOV 7)

rooks.cause: not noise. The lamp stands beyond the board's left half, so on h1 (far right) the key grazes the crown floor and the crenel walls cast real, hard-edged shadows across it (FOV 7: the back half of the floor is in the wall's shadow, lit tongues through the gaps). At the seat that pattern is 30 x 7 px, i.e. lit/shadow patches of 2-4 px, which TSR resolves as grey/white mottle. Independent of shadow method, sample count, denoiser, bias, source size, GI, AO, reflections and screen percentage. a1's bright patch is direct key light on a crown floor that faces the lamp (persists in every test, a1 floor p99 ~218)
rooks.fix_in_lighting: none without losing the key's piece shadows (the long lamp shadows are the run-6 judge's biggest lighting gain). Not changed
rooks.routes_for_other_owners: board/environment: shallower crown floor or bevelled/rounded crenel tops on the rook mesh (fewer, larger shadow shapes); materials: a crown-floor mask that darkens and roughens the floor (the cavity AO is ~0.9 there because the floor is open to the sky) so lit and shadowed patches converge

gown.cause: not shadow noise: the dither is in the G-buffer normal (k_normal capture, C7-gown.jpg): MI_PatientJacket = rough_linen at tiling 5, a sub-pixel weave normal map at the seat distance. It shows as salt-and-pepper wherever the gown is not in direct light. Same with VSM, with Lamp_Opponent's shadow off, at 83/100% TSR
gown.request_to_materials (via lead): MI_PatientJacket: fade the weave normal with pixel footprint (M_TC_PBR DetailFadeInv already exists, C6) or NormalStrength ~0.3 / lower Tiling; the C8m gown grime pass is the natural place
